A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ID2 task, OriPID dataset, and VAE-based retrieval method. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison across the renumbering and relocation of material.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval experiments, baseline evaluations, ablations, robustness tests, and empirical singular-value comparisons in the main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: V2 retains original OriPID experiments and adds results on manually edited images, editing strengths, additional robustness conditions, and alternative editing paradigms.

M1.justification: Both versions learn a linear transformation of fixed VAE embeddings using CosFace and use the transformed embeddings for retrieval. The implementation and loss in Section 4 remain unchanged; the new convolution and attention variants are experimental comparisons.

E1.justification: V2 adds SEED-Data-Edit evaluation on human Photoshop edits, substantially extending coverage beyond diffusion-generated images. Appendix G also extends alternative editing-paradigm tests to EDICT and Plug-and-Play. Resizing, watermarking, and varying editing strengths introduce additional input conditions while the original OriPID coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The OriPID comparator sets remain unchanged. However, v1 Table 9's Circle loss, SoftMax, CosFace, IBN-Net, TransMatcher, and QAConv-GS rows disappear from the corresponding InstructPix2Pix/IP-Adapter comparison in v2 Table 11. V2 Table 7 adds convolution and attention alternatives to the linear transformation.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a deduplicated manual-edit test with 10,274 query-origin pairs and 1,000,000 distractors, a test-strength sweep from 0.1 to 1.0 with training strength held fixed, and resizing/watermarking controls. The original OriPID splits, metrics, and stated training setup remain unchanged. Newly disclosed benchmark generation parameters do not establish a change to those existing experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds systematic editing-strength sensitivity and high-strength failure examples (Appendix D), convolution/attention ablations (Table 7), and resizing/watermarking robustness tests (Figure 7). It also adds successful retrieval examples. Conversely, v1 Figure 7's training-epoch cosine-similarity analysis is removed. Existing encoder, loss, rank, and MLP-depth ablations are retained, with their discussion largely relocated.

E5.justification: Table 1 in both versions reports the same means and standard deviations from ten repetitions. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practices accompany the added experiments.

E6.justification: The original OriPID scores are unchanged, including 88.8% seen and 86.6% unseen mAP. Substantial new results include 86.6% mAP/85.5% accuracy on manual edits (v2 Table 3), 89.0% mAP on EDICT and 99.8% on Plug-and-Play (Table 11), and editing-strength, robustness, and transformation comparisons. These are additional evaluations, not same-setting performance improvements. Alternative-editor baseline scores and the training-similarity curve are removed.

T1.justification: The two theorems, four lemmas, their proofs, and Hypothesis 1 retain the same mathematical content. V1's supplementary proofs move to Appendix A, and the existing broader VAE-based hypothesis remains unproved in both versions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of introducing ID2 and OriPID and providing a theoretically guaranteed, generalizable linear-transformation solution. The headline +31.6% mAP comparison is unchanged. Removing 'Generalizable' from the title does not narrow these retained claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains high-strength failures through the approach toward generation from pure noise, expands the hard-negative explanation through VAE compression and latent overlap, and attributes convolution/attention behavior to underfitting or overfitting. It also interprets the new manual-edit tests as broader practical applicability. The existing distinction between VAE-based generalization and failure on CLIP-based IP-Adapter remains.

D1.justification: V2 Section 5.1 newly discloses per-model editing strengths, SD2 training strength 0.9, and classifier-free guidance scale 7.5. It adds a project URL and describes deduplication and gallery construction for the manual-edit evaluation. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning rate, image resolution, and GPT-4o prompt instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly positions the existing editing procedure as SDEdit and adds references to EDICT, Plug-and-Play, SEED-Data-Edit, and a visual-diffusion replication survey. Adam, PyTorch, and two image-detection references are removed. These are localized positioning and citation changes; the central distinction from image copy detection remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the wording remain intact. V2 moves the detailed ablation discussion from supplementary Section 12 into Section 5.5, reorders and letters the appendices, revises selected explanatory paragraphs, shortens the title, updates affiliations, and adds acknowledgment and impact statements.

P2.justification: V2 expands the robustness figure from two to four panels, adds successful-retrieval and high-strength examples, introduces transformation and editing-strength tables, and adds manual-edit columns to the main comparison. The alternative-editor table is substantially restructured, while the training-similarity plot and paradigm diagrams are removed. Proceedings formatting also changes headers, typography, and placement throughout.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility by disclosing previously unspecified editing parameters and clarifies failure boundaries through the editing-strength sweep. Manual-edit evaluation and added robustness and transformation controls strengthen practical validation. These gains are tempered by removing six alternative-editor baseline rows and the training-similarity analysis; the central method, benchmark results, and theoretical arguments remain unchanged.
